# BrokildApps

A collection of small browser-based apps, native audio plugins and experiments
by Peter Bøggild. The web side is a self-contained static site — no build step,
no server, nothing uploaded. The front page (`index.html`) lists all apps and is
published with GitHub Pages at
[peterboggild.github.io/BrokildApps](https://peterboggild.github.io/BrokildApps/).

The native plugins are built from source with CMake and JUCE 8; the finished
Windows builds are downloadable from each plugin's own landing page.

## How the front page works

The front page is data-driven, so adding an app never means editing HTML:

1. Put the app in its own folder (e.g. `music-apps/my-app/`) with an
   `index.html` inside.
2. Add an `app.json` to that folder with the card's metadata:

   ```json
   {
     "slug": "my-app",
     "name": "My App",
     "description": "One or two sentences for the card.",
     "status": "live",
     "url": "music-apps/my-app/index.html",
     "icon": "wave",
     "preview": "assets/app-previews/my-app.svg",
     "tags": ["music", "phone"]
   }
   ```

   `status` is `"live"` or `"soon"`; `preview` (a 16:9 image in
   `assets/app-previews/`), `note` and `cta` are optional. `icon` picks one of the
   inline icons in `index.html` (`wave`, `note`, `camera`, `keys`, `device`,
   `moon`, `chart`, `more`), and `tags` reference label ids from `manifest.json`.
   `cta` replaces the card's default "Open app →" link text — used by downloadable
   plugins, which are not "opened" the way a browser app is.
   `collection: true` pins the card to the top of the grid.

3. Add the folder name to the `apps` list in `manifest.json`.
4. Run `node tools/sync-site.js` (see below).

### Downloadable plugins

Not everything here runs in the browser. `vst3-apps/` holds native audio plugins:
each one keeps its own landing page (`index.html`) explaining what it is and how
to install it, next to the release `.zip` and its PDF manual, so a visitor can
download it straight from GitHub Pages.

## tools/sync-site.js

The grid is built at runtime by `fetch()`, which no link-preview crawler will
ever run. This script writes the parts that have to exist as static HTML, all of
it derived from `manifest.json` and the `app.json` files — it invents no copy:

- **Open Graph and Twitter Card tags** on every public page, built from that
  page's own `<title>` and `<meta name="description">`, with its `app.json`
  preview as the card image. Without these, a link pasted into Discord, Slack,
  Facebook or iMessage renders as a bare URL.
- **The `<noscript>` list** under the grid on the front page, so the site still
  has working links to every app with scripting off.
- **The app table** in this README.

```sh
node tools/sync-site.js          # write
node tools/sync-site.js --check  # exit 1 if anything is stale
```

Run it after changing `manifest.json`, any `app.json`, or a page's title or
description. It is idempotent.

Two things it needs to know about:

- The published base URL is the `SITE` constant at the top of the script. This
  repo has no `CNAME`, so the site is served from the default project-pages URL;
  if a custom domain is ever added, change that one line and re-run.
- Crawlers will not render an SVG as a preview image. Where a card's art is an
  SVG, keep a PNG of the same frame beside it and the script will prefer it.

## Tests and CI

Every engine has an offline bench: plain C++17, no JUCE, no audio device. They
render real audio and read the numbers off it rather than asserting, and they
run from a terminal, which is why they also run on a CI runner.

| Workflow | What it gates |
|----------|---------------|
| `.github/workflows/engines.yml` | BWFX (409 checks), Rite of Passage (303), Legion (113) and a DSW compile gate. One push to any engine path runs all four, because BWFX is compiled into every plugin. |
| `.github/workflows/clone-wars.yml` | The BWFX bench, the Clone Wars render test and the DSP audit, then the Windows plugin build. A manual dispatch also commits the release zip the site serves. |

Run any of them locally the same way CI does:

```sh
cd BrokildWorldFX/test && g++ -O2 -std=c++17 -I../src -I../modules \
    bench.cpp ../src/*.cpp ../modules/*.cpp -o bwfxtest && ./bwfxtest

cd rite-of-passage && cmake -S test -B test/build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    && cmake --build test/build && ./test/build/roptest

cd vocal-harmonizer && cmake -S test -B test/build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    && cmake --build test/build && ./test/build/legiontest
```

## Serving it

The apps use `fetch()` and (for Photo Synth) `AudioWorklet`, so the site must
be served over http(s) — GitHub Pages, or locally:

```sh
npx http-server -p 8080 .
```
